Historical and genealogical research dossier

A historical life reconstructed source by source.

This public research project examines the life and hotel career associated with the names Sylvester Hermann Gottlieb and S. H. Gottlieb, while keeping evidence, uncertainty, and conflict visible.

Read the working biography Browse 18 sources
Identity noteOpen question

The identification of the hotelier S. H. Gottlieb with Vienna-born Sylvester Hermann Gottlieb is a working hypothesis, not a conclusive identification.

Sources: SRC-001, SRC-002, SRC-003, SRC-008, SRC-009, SRC-011

Caution: Do not merge the two person records without a municipal or other person-level record linking the full name and birth information to the hotel career.

Documented anchors

What the evidence currently supports

The strongest findings are presented with their qualifications and source IDs intact.

CLAIM-SAVOY-1922 Verified direct

A 1922 Swiss travel guide lists S. H. Gottlieb as director of Savoy-Baur en Ville in Zürich.

Sources: SRC-001

Conflicts with: CLAIM-SAVOY-SECONDARY-GOTTLIEB-1910-1918, CLAIM-SAVOY-SECONDARY-GIGER-1918-1926

Caution: This identifies S. H. Gottlieb, but does not by itself prove that he was Sylvester Hermann Gottlieb.

CLAIM-BAUR-POSTCARD Verified direct

A cataloged promotional postcard associates the wording 'Direktion S.H. Gottlieb' with Baur en Ville.

Sources: SRC-002

Caution: Do not assign an exact year or infer more than the catalog wording establishes.

CLAIM-BIRTH-VIENNA-1871 User supplied

Genealogical research identifies Sylvester Hermann Gottlieb as born in Vienna in 1871.

Sources: SRC-011

Caution: The original baptismal entry is not incorporated. Do not add an exact date, parish, parents, or address.

CLAIM-MESSMER-1934 Previously verified

Earlier research found a 1934 telephone-directory association between Hotel Messmer and S. H. Gottlieb.

Sources: SRC-009

Caution: Do not infer that Gottlieb was alive throughout 1934, personally owned the property, lived at the hotel, or died after a particular date. Directory publication lag is possible.

Research priority

Connect the initials to the person.

The highest-value next record is a Zürich municipal registration card. It may connect the full name, Vienna birth information, addresses, and hotel career in one person-level source.
